text:
alex_c: Heads up — hitting a parity bug between Node SDK and REST for route creation + autoscale. REST accepts `autoscale: { min: 1, max: 4 }` but Node SDK returns 400 with `unknown field 'autoscale'`

maria: ugh, repro steps?

alex_c: repro in sample-app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/tree/main/route-config (quick snippet)

alex_c: ```js
// node SDK v0.9.2
await client.routes.create({
  name: 'chat-route',
  model: 'gpt-medium',
  autoscale: { min: 1, max: 4 }
})
// -> 400 Bad Request: unknown field 'autoscale'
```

alex_c: curl equivalent works:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" -d '{"name":"chat-route","model":"gpt-medium","autoscale":{"min":1,"max":4}}'
```

sam: I saw a similar one last week but it was `scaling_policy` vs `autoscale` param naming mismatch. Could be an SDK param rename that wasn't mapped to server-side schema.

tia: Can you paste the full SDK stack trace? might be a validation layer in the client serialiser.

alex_c: stacktrace: `Error: 400 Bad Request - validation_error: unknown field autoscale` — looks like request payload from SDK doesn't include autoscale in JSON. I dumped the outgoing payload and it literally omits the key.

maria: interesting — maybe the TS type is optional and gets stripped because of `undefined` vs `null`? Are you on tsconfig with `skipLibCheck`?

sam: also check auth/retry behavior: our REST client retries on 429 -> fallback model, but SDK retry policy might be swallower or adds jitter. Could be masking a different error upstream.

alex_c: confirmed: sending `autoscale: null` via SDK includes it and server accepts it, but that's not acceptable fix. Repro attached.

maria: thanks. I'll triage. If it's client-side serialisation bug, we should patch in 0.9.3.

dev-bot: Created issue #234 in redwood/inference-sdk: "node SDK: route autoscale field omitted in payload" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/234 :robot_face:

sam: will add an e2e test in CI to post a route with autoscale and assert server gets the key. Also add a parity test comparing SDK payload vs raw REST curl.

tia: small note — we should also check Python SDK because a lot of infra assumes `autoscale` is present for Dedicated orchestrator.

alex_c: thanks — low effort workaround for now is to call REST directly from sample-app until SDK patch lands. Posting a short PR for the sample-app to switch to curl. :+1:

maria: marking this as P1 for SDK parity backlog. I'll assign and include a changelog note.

alex_c: thanks all. I'll update the sample app PR and link the test once CI green.
